provenance: User-provided written breakdown of a manually edited reel. No finished video inspected. Times are reference observations, NOT source-audio cue measurements.
rules: Dynamic means progression of relevant imagery, typography and explanatory scenes, not recurring camera zooms or filling every second.

Build an editorial arc: identity archive, condition anatomy, symptoms, treatment process, outcome qualification, treatment options, advocacy, supplied branding. Adapt this arc to the actual story; do not force every module into every video.

Evaluate every concrete visual opportunity, but group related steps into one readable accumulating list or process scene. A diagram can evolve for eight seconds without replacing it with unrelated stock.
Use authentic named-person photographs/posters for biography. Generic patients cannot depict that person. Missing verified assets remain explicit gaps.
Preserve deliberate static A-roll for explanation, qualifications, uncertainty and emotional delivery. Never insert automatic source-camera reframes as filler.
Motion must serve the asset: reveal a diagram connection, accumulate a list, transition between related archive images. Half-screen imagery remains still; no entrance animation, pan or zoom.

Ordinary subtitles remain static, three words per box per the user preference. Reference karaoke is not permission to change subtitles. Titles remain verbatim complete spoken phrases with noun-level audio anchors.
Reference medical wording and illustrative graphics are not evidence. Verify terminology, identity, licensing and disease-specific applicability; preserve remission-versus-cure qualifications.

Do not copy reference timecodes to raw footage. Resolve each scene to actual source speech and mark uncertain alignment. Unsupported diagram or collage renderers must be reported as gaps, never replaced silently with generic footage.
SFX follows a specific transition or animation; highlight sound only accompanies a real highlight. No sound on every graphic.
